notes.spec_basis: Master Spec v02.229 14-studio-creative-suite.md STU-VID-036 (:23870-23876). Vendor parity UNVERIFIED (D5).
declared_readings: Studio-minted, not in the spec: schema id hsk.studio.track_display@1, token track_display, the six command ids track_display.switches.set, .height.set, .expand_all, .minimize_all, .height_preset.save, .height_preset.recall, code invalid_height, and every Rust and wire name beyond the clause's words.

Defaults, none stated by the clause, vendor parity UNVERIFIED (D5): every on/off switch on, so nothing is hidden by default; video_thumbnails head_only; waveforms shown, logarithmic, not rectified; every track kind 48.

Height unit is logical pixels. Bounds 16..=4096. Minimize-all sets 16, expand-all sets 200, both for every kind. They set values, they are not toggles and keep no prior heights; undo or a preset brings those back. UNVERIFIED (D5).
Audio and video fade handles and audio and video keyframes are one switch per medium, so 18 switches. A single-switch reading is served by setting both.

Audio waveforms hold shown, scaling and rectified. Scaling is one choice of two members, logarithmic or dynamic, from the clause's wording; there is no linear member because the clause declares none. MT-33739 step 1 calls these flags, and its case toggles rectified with both scales, which this shape serves.
'Per kind' means the four members of Folio's TrackKind: video, audio, caption, submix.

Height presets live on the sequence's entry, because the clause makes this state per sequence. A preset has a key-grammar preset_id, unique in the entry, and a name that need not be unique, the sequence preset's shape. Recall is by id. No delete command, the clause states none; a records step can drop one.
A command that does not change what a sequence resolves to adds no entry and is no revision; its report says changed false. Otherwise a sequence without an entry starts from the defaults.

All six commands read the entry, so all are refused folio_rejected or budget_exceeded while it is invalid, on every sequence. As with settings, a bad entry stops display commands, not the file or other commits. A step that does not name it leaves its bytes alone.

Bytes that do not parse and a repeated token cannot be quoted (value_conflict); an explicit set_track_display_records is the way out, the lead's accepted reading for settings. The undo of a step that replaced an invalid entry is refused folio_rejected, also as settings.
A step quoting invalid records unchanged with nothing else changing is no change, not a refusal: the existing no-op check runs first. With anything else changing it is folio_rejected.
resolved_track_displays sends no Observe frame, as the other typed reads do not.

Bounds: at most MAX_TRACK_DISPLAY_ENTRIES (64, equal to MAX_SEQUENCES) entries, inert ones included, 64 presets per entry, names at most 128 bytes, wire form at most MAX_TRACK_DISPLAY_INPUT_BYTES (1 MiB) whatever the caller's budget allows, and Budget::input_bytes when that is lower. A new entry at the entry limit is refused budget_exceeded, on a command or a step; removing an inert entry makes room. Studio's bounds.

Lead decision, Studio reading of a clause silent on a removed sequence, vendor parity UNVERIFIED (D5): display state is a view preference and blocks no document edit or undo. A multicam or records step that removes a sequence, and a resync to a document without it, commit and do not touch the entry. A timeline step cannot remove a sequence: it edits one value under one id.

An inert entry is an entry naming a sequence the document does not hold. It is valid, not noted as a loss, not refused on read, and saved byte-identically. Only the reference is narrowed: its heights, preset ids and names, and its uniqueness are still checked. This narrowing is for this record set only.

resolved_track_displays lists the document's sequences only. inert_track_display_entries lists inert entries whole, read-only, in stored order, and refuses while the entry is invalid. Stored order is the order of the record set, so a commit that replaces the records can change it.

A command cannot edit an inert entry: it answers sequence_missing. A records step can remove or rewrite one. A sequence that comes back has its display state again, with no prune and no extra inverse, because the entry never left.

Consequence of the decision, not tested: a new sequence created with the id of an inert entry takes that entry's display state, since the id is the only link. Sequence ids are the caller's, so this depends on the caller not reusing them.

F-R55-4.a: Not reintroduced: a sequence without an entry resolves to declared defaults, which is state and not a gap, and resolved_track_displays lists every sequence with stored true or false.
F-R55-4.b: Replaced by the lead's decision: a stale reference no longer exists for this record set. An entry naming an absent sequence is inert, listed by inert_track_display_entries, and stops nothing. Other invalid forms open, refuse on read and stop display commands only.
F-R55-4.c: Not reintroduced: a created sequence gets no entry and resolves to the defaults (an_entry_already_invalid_does_not_hold_a_removal_up_and_a_new_sequence_resolves_to_the_defaults).
F-R55-4.d: Not reintroduced: the entry copies no document value except the sequence id (the_records_hold_no_copy_of_a_document_value).
